idiom_name: Boost.DLL shared_library symbol lookup over the platform loader (POSIX dlopen/dlsym fallback)
implementation_notes: C++ keeps the loader as the mediating instance but gives it RAII lifetime: boost::dll::shared_library loads a library by name (with load_mode policies for search paths and platform decorations) and exposes symbol lookup whose result is tied to the library object, so a resolved function cannot outlive the library that defines it - the classic pattern's handle-lifetime problem disappears into the type system. Where Boost is unavailable, POSIX dlopen/dlsym still work but leave lifetime and error handling to the programmer (NULL plus dlerror()). The full role structure (lookup service, registry, binding cache) is only needed when names must be resolved repeatedly against a changing set of providers; for a fixed plugin set, load once at startup and keep the handles in a registry keyed by name.
pitfalls: A symbol (or a function pointer obtained from it) must not outlive the shared_library object; destroying the library while callbacks are still registered is the C++ stale-binding crash.
Load failures and missing symbols surface as boost::system::system_error (Boost.DLL) or NULL plus dlerror() (POSIX); resolution errors must be handled at the boundary, not by terminating the process.
Load-mode and visibility flags (RTLD_GLOBAL/RTLD_LOCAL, Boost load_mode options) decide symbol visibility, so one plugin can accidentally satisfy another plugin's lookups.
